Lucia opens a package. I sit with one leg crossed and scroll through my phone, asking Lucia what to eat. "Let's have noodles," I say. "I don't know what to eat," I add. Lucia thinks, adjusts her glasses, and replies, "Zhajiangmian." I reply, "Zhajiangmian it is. OK." I keep scrolling to compare dishes, then stand up and head outside.

[DAY4 17:49:32 - DAY4 17:50:00]
I look at the Meituan app, shaking my leg as I browse and scroll to decide what to order. "For dinner, do we have anything? Have we missed any traditional Chinese food?" I ask. I'm in the room continuing to browse which takeout to order, trying to figure out what I want to eat. Lucia replies, "It's all good, you can just cut the big pieces." Lucia adds, "Then cut them down and keep modifying."

[DAY1 19:15:00 - DAY1 19:15:30]
I ask everyone, "What are we eating? What should we order for takeout tonight?" I notice everyone's busy and no one answers. Lucia asks, "What are we eating tonight?" I look at my phone and say, "BBQ, haha." I check my phone again. Tasha says, "We must write it down." I ask, "What about rice?" Tasha says, "Okay, just write it down like that." I say, "Rice with toppings." I see many items available for delivery but I'm still unsure what to eat. I suggest, "Yoshinoya noodles," then "Salmon." Lucia says, "All are fine." I suggest "grilled whole fish" and "snail noodles" and note luosifen and other takeout options. Lucia asks, "Is the ventilation in this room good for snail noodles?"

I turn my head to the right. Lucia: "And I was really shocked when it came up." Lucia: "How do you drink this?" Lucia: "Haha." I walk forward, smiling. "Yes," I say. Shure: "Let's start lunch now." I carry my laptop into the bedroom and toss it onto the bed. "Let's order takeout for lunch," I say. I turn right and walk into the living room. "What should we order?" I ask. I long to go outside. I take out my phone and type on it. Shure: "Let's take a look." Shure: "What should we eat?" "Okay," I say. "Meituan takeout," I say. Shure: "Meituan takeout delivers everything fast." I adjust my glasses with my left hand and hold my phone. I walk forward.

Shure hands me a card related to the object, which I inspect as Lucia and Katrina discuss the pressure effects on flower petals and how dehydration causes shrinking. Following their suggestions, I place the card on a table in the computer room and consider using tissue to protect the petals. After interacting with them, I move the stool and kick an object into the computer room, then check my phone while continuing the conversation.

As I prepare to go upstairs, I discuss with Lucia and Katrina the difficulty of reconstructing a flower shape by pressing petals and the whereabouts of other people. I decide to inquire further and head upstairs to speak with Tasha. I ask Tasha what she is doing, and she mentions that others seem inactive. I instruct her to tidy up and decorate the room with pressed flowers, suggesting we also play with the dog. We talk about a delivery and the solar term Grain Rain; I explain its significance and use my phone and GPT to look up related traditions and medicinal products.

While continuing the conversation with Tasha about Grain Rain and food preferences, I propose ordering three lunch boxes for lunch. Lucia comments on the suitability of pressing small flowers, and Tasha questions if I want to open a shop. She picks up a flower and sits beside me as I indicate I will leave the pressing task to her. The interactions conclude with planning for lunch and ongoing discussion about flower pressing and decoration.
